newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan - regulation can work with market forces.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan - regulation can work with market forces.

text.p: Bank regulators must work with market forces, rather than against them, to design and apply rules that make financial institutions more efficient, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Thursday.

"The folly of attempting to legislate or regulate against the primal forces of the market" was one of the most fundamental lessons banking regulators have learned, Greenspan said in a speech prepared for delivery to a banking conference sponsored by the regional Chicago Fed bank.
A text of his remarks was issued in advance in Washington.
Greenspan said effective regulation should recognise and employ investors' and manager's wishes to maximize profits.
"As financial transactions become increasingly rapid and complex, I believe we have no choice but to harness market forces, as best we can, to reinforce our supervisory objectives," Greenspan said.
He said that a requirement for increased disclosure of risk management practises by banks was "a significant step" in applying measures to enhance market discipline.
It gives investors not only the incentive but the means to reward good bank performance or to penalize banks that have inferior standards because they must reveal them.

The Fed chief also said that regulation should try to simulate what would be the private market's response to financial institutions' actions. That means it must be flexible and ready to adapt to changing conditions.
"Such a principle implies that we avoid locking ourselves into formulaic, one-size-fits-all approaches to measuring and affecting bank safety and soundness," Greenspan said.

For example, if a bank develops better internal systems for managing market, credit and operating risks, then supervisory policies should be able to become tailored to meet the bank's specific needs, he suggested.

If market forces are driving financial firms toward centralized decision-making on operational issues like risk management and pricing, then it will be difficult and impractical for regulators to use a decentralized approach to regulation, Greenspan said.
